newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE concerned over U.S. vote on Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: UAE concerned over U.S. vote on Jerusalem.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates has said a U.S. House of Representatives recommendation to President Bill Clinton to reaffirm that Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital cast doubts over Washington's neutrality in the Middle East peace process.

An official source said the move "defies the feelings of the Islamic nation and conflicts with the resolutions of the United Nations and the UN Security Council on the Israeli occupation and holy Jerusalem".

It also "casts doubts on the credibility and the neutrality of the United States in its capacity as one of the co-sponsors of the Middle East peace process, and encourages Israel to be more intransigent and arrogant."
The comments were carried by the state news agency WAM on Sunday night.

Israel, which captured Arab East Jerusalem in 1967 and annexed it in a move unrecognised by the international community including the United States, has welcomed Tuesday's 406-17 vote, which does not oblige Clinton to act.
Arabs regard East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.

In October 1995, the U.S. Senate and the House passed the Jerusalem Embassy Act which states as a matter of U.S. policy that Jerusalem should remain "the undivided capital of Israel" and that the American embassy should be moved there by May 1999.
But recognising the volatility of the issue of Jerusalem, it allowed Clinton to suspend the embassy's move from Tel Aviv for six-month periods.
